data.title: U.K. Unemployment Unchanged Ahead of BOE Meeting — Update
data.description:
By Don Nico Forbes

U.K. unemployment was unchanged in the three months through July, with the labor market showing continued signs of softness ahead of a Bank of England meeting this week.

The unemployment rate was 4.9%, unchanged from the three months through June, according to data released Tuesday by the Office for National Statistics. This was in line with a consensus of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal, and remains close to a five-year high.

The number of payrolled employees continued to fall, particularly in the retail and hospitality sectors, while vacancies remain at their lowest level outside the pandemic period for more than a decade, the ONS said.

With the U.K. continuing to face considerable economic uncertainty, employers have preferred to wait and see before committing to further hiring, said Yael Selfin, an economist at KPMG U.K.

"People just don't want to hire," she said. "Uncertainty means vacancies are low. They were waiting to see before engaging."

Annual wage growth, excluding bonuses, came in at 3.5%, in line with the prior period and economists' views, the data showed.

The figures come ahead of the Bank of England's interest-rate decision Thursday, with the central bank widely expected to leave its key rate at 3.75%, although markets are increasingly pricing in the possibility of a rate increase ahead as inflation risks have risen.

Inflation data for August, due Wednesday, is expected to show annual price growth rising above 3% compared with 2.9% in July, driven by energy prices as the war in Iran drags on.

Still, core inflation is seen stable at 2.6%, with few signs that higher energy prices are feeding through to other areas of the economy. Alongside stable wage growth, core inflation data could rein in expectations for rate hikes going forward.

"The labor market remains too weak for wage growth to follow consumer prices higher," said Andrew Wishart, an economist at Berenberg.

"As a result, we think that the BOE only has to hike once rather than four times as investors currently predict," he said.

Write to Don Nico Forbes at don.forbes@wsj.com

data.title: ZAWYA: Oman: VA Group secures land rights for Muttrah waterfront development
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Muscat – VA Group, an international real estate developer, has secured long-term land rights in Muttrah for its development project. It is the first international company that will deliver a phase within the Port Sultan Qaboos Waterfront Masterplan. The project is being advanced in close partnership with Omran Group.

As a part of the Port Sultan Qaboos Waterfront Masterplan, VA Group will deliver its Muttrah Waterfront Development. While full details have not yet been disclosed, the project is designed as a mixed-use, master-planned destination combining premium residences with world-class public spaces, a signature waterfront promenade, parks, sports and leisure facilities, and carefully curated retail and cultural attractions. The total development site area is around 18.5 hectares, equivalent to approximately 23 football fields.

Conceived to complement Muttrah’s rich cultural and historical identity, VA Group’s development will contribute to the district’s long-term transformation and revitalisation, boosting Oman’s tourism offering and enriching lifestyle experiences along the capital’s waterfront, VA Group stated.

‘Muttrah Waterfront Development will represent a rare opportunity to reside where authentic history and modernity intertwine amid ancient fortresses, a vibrant community rhythm, and the unmistakable character of a district that has welcomed the world for generations.’

Mohamed Saif Al Shaqsi, Executive Director for the GCC Region at VA Group Oman, said, “To develop in Muttrah, within the Port Sultan Qaboos Waterfront Masterplan, is to carry an extraordinary responsibility and, above all, a privilege. The property here carries not only an address, but also historical weight. We will soon announce the name and details of this unique project, delivering something enduring and worthy of this place and its people.”

As a strategic partner of Omran Group, VA Group supports initiatives aligned with Oman Vision 2040. Muttrah Waterfront Development addresses key pillars of the national agenda, including economic diversification and long-term investment attraction through world-class urban planning and sustainable infrastructure design, positioning Oman as a premier tourism destination, and enhancing quality of life by creating integrated communities with vibrant public spaces and cultural environments.

Furthermore, VA Group said it supports Oman’s in-country value (ICV) principles, generating significant direct and indirect employment opportunities across the development lifecycle and ensuring lasting benefits for Oman’s economy and society.

data.title: From schoolyard sweets trader to Africa's richest man, Dangote eyes his biggest deal yet
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dangote built his fortune from sugar, rice, cement and salt
  • Launching Africa's biggest-ever IPO for Nigeria refinery
  • Deal marks high water mark in decades-long business career

By Duncan Miriri and MacDonald Dzirutwe

More than half a century after launching his business career selling candy to classmates in northern Nigeria, serial entrepreneur Aliko Dangote is preparing the biggest stock market listing Africa has ever seen.

Launched on Monday, the sale of $1.6 billion worth of shares in his giant Lagos oil refinery — an initial public offering that will see the refinery list in Nigeria in November — values the company at $47 billion.

The deal is the culmination of Dangote's more than a decade-long effort to develop a mega-refinery now ranked among the world's 10 largest. It also marks the peak to date in a career that has seen him rise from schoolyard sweets merchant to Africa's richest man.

And the 69-year-old has no plans to stop there, with proceeds from the IPO destined for an expansion drive that will double the Nigerian facility's capacity and launch a new refinery project on the other side of the continent in Kenya.

SUGAR, CEMENT, RICE AND SALT

Born in Nigeria's northern state of Kano in 1957, Dangote was raised principally by his maternal grandfather, whom he has credited with encouraging his interest in business.

"When you are raised by an entrepreneurial parent or grandparent you pick up that aspiration," he said in a 2015 interview. "It makes you be much more aggressive, to think anything is possible."

Reuters was unable to secure an interview with Dangote despite repeated requests.

After graduating from university in Egypt, he began trading sugar and rice in 1977 with a loan from a relative.

He incorporated Dangote Industries, in which he now holds 85%, in the early 1980s, building it into a conglomerate spanning sugar, cement and salt that operates in more than a dozen African countries.

Dangote's personal fortune, currently estimated at between $31 billion and $35 billion, grew on the back of his lucrative cement business.

Government policies that fostered domestic cement production helped Nigeria become largely self-sufficient in the essential building material, though they also fuelled criticism that limited competition kept prices high.

ECONOMIC FOLK HERO TO SOME, VILLAIN TO OTHERS

With wealth came influence.

Already two decades ago, U.S. diplomats in a leaked 2005 cable said he was considered an "economic folk hero" by some but was viewed as a "villain" by others, who suspected he used his proximity to politics to further his business.

"The truth resides somewhere between these caricatures," they wrote.

People who have met him often describe Dangote as unusually reserved for someone of his wealth and influence.

"He is a man with an instinct for opportunity and the discipline to turn ambition into something real," said Kenyan business owner and author Gina Din Kariuki.

"But that is not what stayed with me, it was his humility."

Shunning flashy displays, he often drives himself. And despite periodically threatening to buy his favourite soccer team — London's Arsenal — he prides himself on keeping the bulk of his fortune in Nigeria.

"He is one hell of a hard worker, who knows all the bolts and nuts of each of his business," said Bismarck Rewane, CEO of Lagos-based Financial Derivatives Company Ltd, who has known Dangote for more than two decades.

"Some people call him a control freak. I see it as passion to see things done."

Not everyone is a fan, however, and local fuel traders in Nigeria accuse Dangote of leveraging political ties to squeeze out competitors.

He argues his 700,000-barrels-per-day refinery can now meet Nigeria's fuel needs and is battling in court to end imports. Regulators, however, have warned of a risk of a fuel supply monopoly.

Neither Dangote nor officials at the Dangote Group responded to requests for comment on the allegations.

But he has said the listing should help counter monopoly concerns.

"They will now say we have shares, so let everybody have a part of it," he told a conference last year.

The Iran war's stark exposure of oil-rich but refinery-poor Africa's dependence on fuel imports brought heightened attention to Dangote's stated mission of pushing the continent towards self-sufficiency.

After the conflict sparked concerns over fuel supplies, Kenya approached Dangote about building an East African refinery, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

Two months later, Dangote joined Kenyan and Ugandan leaders to announce the project, which he said will break ground this month.

data.title: Australian shares close at over three-month low as miners, banks slide ahead of Fed decision
data.description:
Key points:
  • AXJO ends at over three month low
  • Miners post fourth straight session of losses
  • Investors await Fed's cash rate decision due later this week

By Aamir Khalid

Australian shares closed at a more-than-three-month low on Tuesday, dragged down by commodity stocks and banks as investors awaited the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate decision later this week, while higher bond yields and inflation concerns also weighed.

The S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.9% to close at 8,672.50 points, its lowest close since early June. It rose 0.1% on Monday.

The U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting starts on Wednesday, and investors are wary that stubborn inflation and higher oil prices could warrant a further tightening of interest rates.

That increases the odds of the Reserve Bank of Australia needing to maintain a hawkish stance, especially as renewed hostilities in the Middle East add to uncertainty and keep risk appetite subdued.

"The Fed meeting kicks off tomorrow with a high probability of a 25 bps hike ... For Australian equities that means growth multiples compress, rate-sensitive REITs and utilities underperform," said Emanuel Ajay Datt, managing director of Datt Group.

"Renewed Middle East tensions and Iranian attacks on Gulf shipping have pushed oil prices higher and investors appear to be taking risk off the table."

In Sydney, miners fell 2.3%, their fourth straight session of losses, dragged down by lower iron ore prices, with BHP and Rio Tinto losing more than 2% each.

Banks lost 1.1%, with the "Big Four" lenders trading in the red. That, said Datt, suggested investors were focusing more on a potential deterioration in credit quality than the boost to net interest margins from higher rates.

Gold stocks fell 3.1% and energy stocks dropped 1.6%

Bucking the trend, health stocks gained 1.5% and technology stocks ended 0.3% higher.

Across the Tasman Sea, the New Zealand benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index fell 0.6% to 13,484.22 points.

data.title: Juniper Green Energy Completes 75 MW Hybrid Project In Maharashtra
data.description:
The final 10 MW wind capacity has been commissioned, taking the company’s operational portfolio to around 2,604 MWp and 500 MWh of BESS.

Juniper Green Energy has fully commissioned a 75 MW wind-solar hybrid power project in Maharashtra, strengthening its renewable generation portfolio as developers increasingly combine wind and solar assets to improve utilisation and supply reliability.

The final 10 MW wind capacity was commissioned on September 9, 2026, through wholly owned subsidiary Juniper Green Spark Ten, with officials from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) witnessing the commissioning. The commissioning takes Juniper Green Energy’s aggregate operational capacity, including subsidiaries, to around 2,604 MWp, alongside approximately 500 MWh of battery energy storage capacity. The company has been expanding its portfolio through a mix of solar, wind, hybrid and storage projects.

Hybrid Capacity Gains

The project reflects a broader shift in India’s renewable energy market towards hybrid configurations, which can reduce the intermittency associated with standalone solar generation. MSEDCL’s contracted hybrid portfolio stood at 4,344 MW as of April 2025, while only 300 MW had been commissioned at that point, highlighting the substantial pipeline of hybrid capacity awaiting execution. The 75 MW project is part of Juniper’s broader expansion in Maharashtra. The company has previously commissioned solar components of hybrid projects in the state ahead of their scheduled commercial operation dates, reflecting an emphasis on faster project execution.

Renewables Push

Industry experts say the growing deployment of wind-solar hybrids is being driven by the need to improve renewable power availability, optimise transmission infrastructure and provide a more balanced generation profile across the day. The trend is also gaining importance as India seeks to scale non-fossil generation while managing rising electricity demand. Hybrid projects, increasingly supported by battery storage, are expected to play a larger role in providing more predictable renewable power to utilities and commercial consumers.

data.title: Aster Guardians Award Names Agimol Pradeep Global Nursing Winner
data.description:
UK-based Indian-origin nurse receives USD 250,000 prize after emerging from more than 134,000 registrations across 214 countries and economies

Nurse Agimol Pradeep from the United Kingdom has been named the winner of the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026, receiving the USD 250,000 prize at a ceremony in Kochi on 12 September. Pradeep, a Senior Transplant Coordinator at King’s College Hospital and Honorary Senior Lecturer at the University of Salford, emerged as the winner from more than 134,000 registrations submitted by nurses across 214 countries and economies.

The award was presented by Shri V. D. Satheesan, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Keralam, alongside Dr. Azad Moopen, Founder and Executive Chairman, Aster DM Quality Care Ltd, Alisha Moopen, Executive Director, Aster DM Quality Care Ltd, T.J. Wilson, Director, Aster DM Quality Care, and Varun Khanna, Managing Director and Group CEO of Aster DM Quality Care Ltd.

Advancing Nursing Impact

The ceremony also featured a special message from Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization, who congratulated the finalists and recognised nurses’ contribution to healthcare worldwide.

Pradeep has focused her career on addressing healthcare inequities, particularly among minority communities. After identifying the impact of donor shortages on South Asian patients awaiting transplants, she co-founded the Upahaar initiative, which has registered more than 10,000 stem-cell donors.

“I have seen how a shortage of ethnically matched donors can leave patients from minority communities waiting longer for a life-saving transplant,” Pradeep said. She plans to use half of her prize money to expand organ and stem-cell donation initiatives through Upahaar, while also supporting nursing education and training.

Dr. Azad Moopen said Pradeep’s achievement reflects the “expertise, courage, compassion and unwavering commitment” that define exceptional nursing, adding that the award aims to recognise and elevate nurses’ contributions globally. Alisha Moopen highlighted Pradeep’s community-led work, saying her efforts in transplantation and organ donation among the UK’s South Asian community had “set a benchmark for many to follow.”

The remaining nine finalists were selected from Sweden, Saudi Arabia, Hong Kong SAR, India, Colombia, Namibia, Nigeria and Papua New Guinea. They included Dr. Aidah Alkaissi, Dinah Sevilla, Dr. Hammoda Abu-Odah, Hindumbi K, Johana Patricia Galvan Barrios, Josephine Nelago Angula, Oluchi Angel Okoi, Peter Fore and Ronald Mario Cañas Rojas.

The finalists underwent a selection process involving Ernst & Young LLP, a Screening Jury and a Grand Jury, with assessments based on professional achievement, leadership, innovation, impact and contributions to nursing.

Since its launch in 2021, the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award has developed into an international platform celebrating nurses driving change across healthcare systems and communities.

data.title: How Warner Bros. Discovery Turned Harry Potter Into A Licensing Machine For Every Category
data.description:
As Harry Potter expands across eyewear, jewellery, travel, food, beauty and lifestyle, marketers explain why the strongest entertainment collaborations build on fandom rather than simply borrowing an IP logo

In the wizarding world, Alohomora is the charm Hermione Granger reaches for whenever a locked door stands between her and the next chapter of the story — a quick flick of the wand, and a new space opens up. Twenty-five years after the first film, Warner Bros. Discovery seems to be running the same charm on the retail map.

Every fresh licensing deal functions like its own Alohomora moment: a category that had nothing to do with wizarding lore; eyewear, biscuits, toothpaste, luggage; suddenly unlocks and the drop sells out within minutes of hitting shelves or e-commerce carts. Harry Potter is no longer just an entertainment property; it has become one of the most versatile licensing engines in the consumer market, and each new door it opens seems to draw the same rush of fans waiting on the other side.

The India Playbook

The India-specific rollout alone tells the story. Lenskart has launched an eyewear line inspired by the four houses and the Chamber of Secrets, while CaratLane has built a fine jewellery collection around the franchise's most recognisable motifs.

Nasher Miles has introduced an exclusive Harry Potter travel and luggage range, and American Tourister has gone further with an extensive school and travel gear line featuring interchangeable Velcro house badges; letting fans wear their house pride quite literally on their sleeve. On the food side, éntisi Chocolatier has rolled out India's first officially licensed luxury Harry Potter chocolate collection, complete with Chocolate Frogs and Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans, while Britannia has introduced Hogwarts-crest biscuits and Kinder Joy has released Quidditch-themed surprise-toy collections.

A Global Ecosystem

Beyond India, the ecosystem is just as expansive. Starbucks ran a multi-market Asia Pacific campaign built around the Honeydukes Bursting Bonbons beverage series and more than 20 pieces of color-changing drinkware, and Tim Hortons launched a Back to Hogwarts menu with limited-edition packaging.

In beauty and personal care, Colgate expanded its Sorting Hat-themed oral care line across Asia Pacific, and Mad Beauty released an Autumn/Winter collection timed to the Back to Hogwarts season. Timex introduced themed watches including the Waterbury Skeleton Automatic, Puma unveiled a house-colour athleisure and footwear collection, and Hasbro signed a multi-year global partnership covering toys, games and interactive play. MINISO, meanwhile, has opened large-format pop-up stores stocking over 300 lifestyle and stationery items.

Why A 25-year-old IP Still Unlocks Every Door

The scale of this activity raises an obvious question: what makes a 25-year-old entertainment IP capable of unlocking categories as disconnected as eyewear, biscuits and toothpaste and having each one clear out almost as fast as it launches?

For Shalini Sharma, Head of Marketing at Piccadily Distilleries, the answer lies in how entertainment properties have transformed into cultural platforms rather than static assets. As she puts it: "Entertainment IPs today have evolved far beyond being properties that brands simply associate with; they have become powerful cultural platforms that enable collaborations across categories, industries and consumer communities.

Over the years, we have seen iconic entertainment franchises create opportunities for brands in fashion, technology, beauty, food and beverage, luxury and lifestyle to find their own interpretation of a shared cultural moment. For Indri, our collaboration with Warner Bros. Discovery around House of the Dragon was an opportunity to bring together two worlds built on craftsmanship, legacy, storytelling and collectability.

Rather than simply borrowing from the world of Westeros, we wanted to create an expression that felt authentic to both the IP and Indri's own identity as a globally ambitious Indian single malt. What makes entertainment collaborations particularly powerful is their ability to introduce a brand to new audiences while giving existing consumers a fresh reason to engage with it.

When approached with relevance and creative integrity, an IP can become a canvas on which brands across very different categories can build distinctive cultural narratives. For us, House of the Dragon allowed Indri to participate in that larger cultural conversation while demonstrating how Indian luxury spirits can confidently engage with some of the world's most iconic entertainment franchises."

Beyond Merchandise: Borrowed Meaning, Not Borrowed Logos

But scale alone does not guarantee resonance, and this is where the risk of an IP tipping into pure merchandising becomes real. Rahul Shukla, Vice President and Chief Sales & Marketing Officer at Titan, frames this as the central discipline behind any successful collaboration: "Here are my two cents on this.

What Harry Potter has managed to do is something only a few IPs pull off - it's stayed a story, not just a product. The moment an IP starts feeling like it's only there to sell a bag or a lipstick, fans switch off immediately. We saw this ourselves at Titan years back, when our kids' watch brand Zoop tied up with Marvel and launched an Iron Man collection timed to the film.

It wasn't just an Iron Man face slapped on a dial — the watch was built around a kid's excitement for that character at that moment, so the product felt like an extension of the fandom, not a cash-in on it. You see the same instinct with brands like boAt tying up with Marvel or Star Wars for their audio range. The product stays the same, but suddenly it's carrying a story people already love.

The Lenskart and Swiss Beauty collaborations with Harry Potter work on that same principle. They're borrowing the emotion of the houses and the wands, and letting it sit naturally on the product. For any category, IP isn't merchandise, it's borrowed meaning. Get that right, and relevance takes care of itself."

The Charm Only Works With Intent

Taken together, both perspectives point to the same underlying shift: entertainment IPs are increasingly functioning less as branding shortcuts and more as shared cultural vocabularies. Every Alohomora moment — a new category, a new drop, a new sell-out, works only because the charm is cast with intent, not just muscle memory. Whether it's a single malt drawing on the mythology of Westeros or an eyewear brand borrowing the emotional weight of Hogwarts houses, the brands succeeding with Harry Potter — and with entertainment collaborations more broadly, are the ones translating fandom into authentic product experiences, not simply stamping a logo onto a shelf.

Ojasvita Trivedi

BW Reporters The author is a trainee correspondent at BW Businessworld.

data.title: ZAWYA: Number of factories in Saudi Arabia surpasses 15,000
data.description:
By Staff Writer

RIYADH — Abdullah Saleh Kamel, chairman of the Federation of Saudi Chambers, revealed that since the launch of Saudi Vision 2030, the number of industrial establishments in Saudi Arabia has risen from 7,000 to more than 15,000 across various economic sectors.

“This growth includes sectors that were not previously licensed before the launch of the Vision, such as military industries, with the number of licensed companies in these sectors now exceeding 347,” he said while addressing the inaugural session of the second edition of the Saudi Industry Forum 2026 at Jeddah Superdome on Monday. The three-day forum is organized by the Federation of Saudi Chambers of Commerce, represented by the National Committee of Industry, in cooperation with the Jeddah Chamber of Commerce.

Kamel highlighted the growth of local and foreign investments in the industry sector, noting that the sector’s contribution to GDP has risen to 16 percent. “The Kingdom has emerged as a leader in several industries, including petrochemicals, machinery and equipment, military industries, food and pharmaceuticals, textiles, and building materials,” he said.

Kamel emphasized that Saudi products have become strong competitors in global markets. “We, in the federation, have witnessed the desire of importers from friendly countries to learn about Saudi products, which was confirmed by the data on the growth of non-oil exports, which has made us leaders locally and internationally. This leadership came with the support of the government of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman, and with the economic resources and competitive advantages that our country possesses. The most important of these leverages are the availability of basic materials, the development of the industrial system through legislation, and the government enablers that have empowered the private sector to enhance its competitive capabilities in the sector, in addition to the existence of advanced infrastructure, and the Kingdom’s proximity to global markets. All of these are due to a leadership that has set a high ceiling for ambition, and a private sector that has proven its ability to invest, grow and compete,” he said.

Regarding the methodology of the Federation of Saudi Chambers, Kamel stated that the federation is striving to establish strategic partnerships with relevant government entities in the industrial sector to achieve the Kingdom’s objectives at both the local and international levels.

“The future requires the private sector to become more capable of attracting and localizing high-quality industries in the Kingdom, fostering innovation and development across various sectors, and leveraging artificial intelligence, Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies, and other enabling factors and changes within the sector. These efforts will help position the Kingdom as a leading industrial power on the global economic map,” he said while emphasizing that the Federation of Chambers remains committed to supporting investors in the Kingdom's industrial sector to achieve Saudi Arabia's goals.

data.title: Wolters Kluwer expands Libra legal AI workspace with authoritative expert content from Kluwer Law International
data.description:
Wolters Kluwer Legal & Regulatory today announced the integration of Kluwer Law International content into Libra by Wolters Kluwer, its all-in-one legal AI workspace. Customers in 11 European countries can now access content from Kluwer Arbitration, Kluwer Competition Law and Kluwer IP Law directly within Libra, further expanding the platform's portfolio of trusted legal content and expert insight.

The addition of Kluwer Law International content builds on Libra's existing legal intelligence capabilities and gives legal professionals access to specialist international expertise across arbitration, competition law and intellectual property law without leaving their workflow. Content can be used alongside the broader Wolters Kluwer legal resources already available within Libra, helping users conduct research, validate arguments and draft documents with greater efficiency and confidence.

“By adding Kluwer Arbitration, Kluwer Competition Law and Kluwer IP Law in Libra, we are expanding the breadth and depth of trusted legal content available to customers," said Linda Nieuwenhuis, VP Growth & Operations Libra by Wolters Kluwer. “Legal professionals can now access even more specialist international content directly within their AI-powered workflow."

Jill Weinstein, Vice President & General Manager, Legal Markets at Wolters Kluwer Legal & Regulatory U.S., added: "The future of legal AI depends on the quality of the knowledge behind it. By bringing Kluwer Law International's specialist content into Libra, we are extending the reach of our authors' expertise and making trusted legal analysis available at the moment our customers need it most."

The integration is designed to benefit multiple customer groups, including existing Libra users who require specialist international legal expertise. Customers can activate the relevant content sets within Libra after purchasing and use them as part of their research, drafting, and review processes.

Wolters Kluwer’s Legal & Regulatory division enables legal and compliance professionals to improve productivity and performance, mitigate risk, and solve complex problems with confidence. Its expert solutions combine deep domain knowledge with advanced technology and services to deliver better outcomes, advanced analytics, and improved productivity for customers.

About Wolters Kluwer

Wolters Kluwer (EURONEXT: WKL) is a global leader in information, software solutions and services for professionals in healthcare; tax and accounting; financial and corporate compliance; legal and regulatory; corporate performance and ESG. We help our customers make critical decisions every day by providing expert solutions that combine deep domain knowledge with technology and services.

Wolters Kluwer reported 2025 annual revenues of €6.1 billion. The group serves customers in over 180 countries, maintains operations in over 40 countries, and employs approximately 21,100 people worldwide. The company is headquartered in Alphen aan den Rijn, the Netherlands.

For more information, visit www.wolterskluwer.com, follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube and Instagram.
